narrativeReportMd:
# Coding R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No hard instance-breaking local Coding changes were found. The same local elements remain with the same names, cardinalities, primitive types, summary flags, and modifier status. The main R4-to-R6 migration risks are conformance/runtime risks: R6 adds a warning invariant discouraging display-only `Coding` values, and it tightens the `Coding.system` comment to say non-special system identifiers should be absolute references.

## Scope
This assessment covers the local `Coding` datatype only. The R6 artifact exists at the same canonical URL, so there is no rename, split, merge, or removal issue. The R4-to-R6 shift from `Element` to `DataType` as the baseDefinition, plus inherited `id` and `extension` details, are out of scope and should be handled by base-artifact reports.

## Main migration themes
Implementers should look for `Coding` fragments that carry only `display` without `code`; R6 validators can now emit warning `cod-1`. Implementers should also review non-absolute `Coding.system` identifiers, because R6 text is clearer that system URIs should be absolute except for defined special cases.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact local finding is `Coding:VALUE_CONSTRAINT:Coding:cod-1`: it is not a hard validation error, but warning-as-error validation pipelines and QA gates can break. `Coding:SEMANTIC_OR_CONFORMANCE_TEXT:Coding.system:absolute-system-uri` is lower impact but important for semantic interoperability.

## Findings requiring human review
Both findings benefit from human review because the real impact depends on local data and validation policy: whether display-only codings are used intentionally, whether warnings fail builds, and whether existing system identifiers are local aliases that need stable absolute URIs.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The R6 warning is a relatively non-disruptive way to discourage unsafe display-only coded data. The `Coding.system` text change is guidance rather than a computable constraint, so it preserves wire compatibility while signaling stronger conformance expectations.

## Follow-up analysis
Review DataType/Element reports for inherited class-hierarchy and base element changes. A corpus scan of real instances would improve prevalence estimates for the two local findings.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No hard local `Coding` instance break was found. The top concerns are the new R6 `cod-1` warning for display-only codings and the stronger absolute-URI guidance for `Coding.system`. The main uncertainty is how often existing data and validation pipelines rely on the now-discouraged patterns.
summary.migrationThemesMd: The migration work is mostly cleanup and policy alignment rather than structural transformation. Existing JSON/XML shape remains stable, but validators, QA gates, and terminology governance should be updated to handle R6's warning on display-only codings and the clearer expectation that code system identifiers be absolute, stable, and unambiguous.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the structural comparison because both primary StructureDefinitions and package indexes were available locally and matched the assigned artifact. Confidence is lower for prevalence and intent because no official diff, change rationale, rendered migration note, or real-world instance corpus was supplied.

findings.title: R6 adds a Coding-level warning against display-only Coding values

oldState.summary: R4 had no Coding-specific warning or invariant that discouraged `display` when `code` was absent.

constraints.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

semanticText.definition: A reference to a code defined by a terminology system.

oldState.narrativeMd: A R4 `Coding` containing `display` but no `code` satisfied the local Coding definition as long as the general Element content rule was met.

newState.summary: R6 adds warning invariant `cod-1`: a Coding SHOULD NOT have a display unless code is also present.

constraints.human: A Coding SHOULD NOT have a display unless a code is also present.  Computation on Coding.display alone is generally unsafe.  Consider using CodeableConcept.text
All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

semanticText.definition: A reference to a code defined by a terminology system.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 validators can report `cod-1` when `display` is populated without `code`; the R6 `Coding.code` and `Coding.display` elements also carry condition markers for this invariant.

facts.oldValue: No local condition on Coding.code or Coding.display
facts.newValue: `cod-1` appears as a condition on Coding.code and Coding.display

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The finding compares the same root `Coding` element and the same child element ids across R4 and R6; only the local warning invariant is new.

impact.impactRationaleMd: `cod-1` is a warning, not an error, so a display-only `Coding` is not made hard-invalid by the base R6 StructureDefinition. The practical break is in validation and runtime policy: systems that fail on warnings, generated validators that surface warnings as exceptions, or QA pipelines that require zero warnings may reject records accepted under R4. The warning also encodes a semantic safety concern because computations on `display` alone are unsafe.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Display text without an actual code can be ambiguous, localized, or stale. If downstream clinical or billing logic treats `display` as coded data, migration can expose or increase semantic safety risk.

justification.inferredGoal: Discourage use of Coding as free text and direct uncoded text toward CodeableConcept.text.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the display-without-code advice non-computable or profile-specific instead of adding a base warning invariant.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: `Coding.display` is not a safe stand-in for `Coding.code`, and R6 makes that safety rule visible to base validators. Because `cod-1` is warning-severity rather than an error and does not change the `Coding` wire shape, the breakage is limited to implementations that escalate warnings or use warnings as release gates. A less-breaking path exists, but it would materially weaken the computable base signal, so this warning-level design is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have been to leave the base `Coding` constraints unchanged and express the same advice only in narrative text, best-practice notes, or profile-level expectations. That would preserve display-only R4 `Coding` instances without even a base warning, but it only partially meets the R6 goal because generic validators and authoring tools could not reliably identify display-only codings across the base ecosystem. This is a weaker base design, not merely a migration-tooling workaround, and its tradeoff is reduced safety/interoperability signaling.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids new base warnings for legacy display-only codings, but loses generic validator and tooling detection of an unsafe pattern.

evidence.detail: R4 root Coding constraints include only inherited `ele-1`; no `cod-1` constraint is present.
R6 adds local warning invariant `cod-1` with expression `code.exists().not() implies display.exists().not()`.
evidence.quote: A Coding SHOULD NOT have a display unless a code is also present.

evidence.detail: R6 marks both `Coding.code` and `Coding.display` as affected by condition `cod-1`.

examples.examplesMd: The first object is an illustrative `Coding` fragment. In R4 it has no Coding-specific warning; in R6 it triggers `cod-1` because `display` exists and `code` does not. If the data is truly free text rather than a display for a code, the usual migration target is the containing `CodeableConcept.text`, shown as a simplified transform fragment.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 makes a previously implicit safety recommendation computable: `Coding.display` should not be used by itself. Existing R4 data that used `Coding` as a convenient display-only container can still be serialized in R6, but it will produce a warning. This can surprise implementers because the element cardinalities did not change and the instance shape still looks compatible.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not an old-valid/new-invalid validation error under the base R6 definition because the new invariant has warning severity. It is nevertheless a compatibility issue for validators, CI pipelines, import jobs, and generated validation layers that escalate warnings. R6 content that satisfies the new warning is representable in R4 because no new element or type is involved.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Scan for `Coding` objects with `display` but no `code`. If an actual code is known, populate `system` and `code` and keep `display` as the code display. If the value is free text, move it to the containing `CodeableConcept.text` or an appropriate profile-specific text element. Update validation policy deliberately so R6 warnings are reviewed without accidentally blocking all legacy records unless that is intended.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change was probably justified because it addresses a known semantic hazard without making the pattern a hard error. A fully backward-compatible alternative would have been narrative guidance only, but that would not help generic validators identify unsafe display-only codings.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review should focus on whether local validation policy treats warnings as failures and whether any display-only codings are intentional legacy text that should migrate to a containing CodeableConcept rather than be given artificial codes.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds a root-level `cod-1` invariant saying a `Coding` SHOULD NOT carry `display` when `code` is absent. This can affect validation pipelines that treat warnings as failures, but it is not an old-valid/new-invalid base instance break because the invariant severity is `warning` and the wire shape of `Coding.code` and `Coding.display` is unchanged. For a display-only exchange, the likely migration work is to move free text to `CodeableConcept.text`, provide an actual code, or accept the warning. The safety/computability rationale is strong: a display string alone is ambiguous and should not be processed as coded meaning.
keyEvidence: R4 `StructureDefinition-Coding.json` root `Coding` constraints include inherited `ele-1` only.
R6 `StructureDefinition-Coding.json` differential adds `cod-1` on `Coding` with severity `warning` and expression `code.exists().not() implies display.exists().not()`.
R6 marks `Coding.code` and `Coding.display` with condition `cod-1`, while both elements remain 0..1 with the same `code` and `string` types.
R4 maturity metadata for Coding shows standardsStatus `normative` and normativeVersion `4.0.0`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Coding is normative in R4, so even warning-level conformance pressure deserves a real compatibility check. The normative status raises the justification burden, but the non-error severity and patient-safety/computability rationale make the burden proportionate.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: warning-level: R4 display-only Codings remain structurally representable in R6, but R6 validators or QA gates that fail on warnings may reject or require cleanup of instances that R4 accepted without this warning.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less disruptive base design would have been prose-only guidance or an IG/profile-specific warning, but that would not give generic validators a computable signal for a broadly unsafe pattern. Keeping the invariant at warning severity is already the less-breaking version of an enforceable constraint.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing impact and alternative judgment: the prior report correctly identifies no hard instance break and a warning/policy migration risk, but I would frame the design as proportionate rather than as a finding needing more standards attention.

findings.title: R6 tightens Coding.system guidance to prefer absolute system identifiers

oldState.summary: R4 says a non-HL7-special URI should reference a definition that establishes the system clearly and unambiguously.

semanticText.comment: The URI may be an OID (urn:oid:...) or a UUID (urn:uuid:...).  OIDs and UUIDs SHALL be references to the HL7 OID registry. Otherwise, the URI should come from HL7's list of FHIR defined special URIs or it should reference to some definition that establishes the system clearly and unambiguously.

oldState.narrativeMd: `Coding.system` was optional `uri` with guidance for clear, unambiguous system identification, but the comment did not explicitly say that the reference should be absolute.

newState.summary: R6 keeps the same element and type but says other system identifiers should be absolute references to a definition.

semanticText.comment: The URI may be an OID (urn:oid:...) or a UUID (urn:uuid:...).  OIDs and UUIDs SHALL be references to the HL7 OID registry. Otherwise, the URI should come from HL7's list of FHIR defined special URIs or it should be an absolute reference to some definition that establishes the system clearly and unambiguously.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 leaves the wire format unchanged but tightens the conformance expectation for non-special code system identifiers by adding the word `absolute`.

facts.oldValue: it should reference to some definition that establishes the system clearly and unambiguously
facts.newValue: it should be an absolute reference to some definition that establishes the system clearly and unambiguously

facts.note: The primitive type did not change; the risk comes from conformance text, not schema shape.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same `Coding.system` element id and path exist in R4 and R6 with unchanged cardinality and type; the only local material delta is the comment text.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The R6 StructureDefinition does not add a computable regex, type change, or invariant requiring absolute URIs, so existing values are not made hard-invalid by the base schema. The risk is semantic and policy-driven: linters, terminology governance checks, or profile authors may now flag local or relative system identifiers as non-conformant with R6 guidance.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Changing or aliasing code system identifiers can affect the identity of codes. Ambiguous local systems can cause clinical, billing, or analytics misclassification if not mapped carefully.

justification.inferredGoal: Strengthen globally resolvable and unambiguous code system identity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 comment wording and add softer base guidance or examples encouraging absolute system identifiers.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable because `Coding.system` defines the namespace for interpreting `Coding.code`, and absolute identifiers reduce ambiguity across servers and organizations. The R6 change is only conformance text: cardinality, type, and computable validation are unchanged, so existing R4-shaped instances remain structurally valid. A softer wording alternative exists, but it would leave more room for relative or local aliases to be treated as acceptable base practice; given the low level of breakage, the clarification is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could have retained the R4 comment text and added examples or non-normative guidance that absolute code system URIs are preferred for interoperable exchange. That would better accommodate legacy local `system` strings, but it only partially meets the goal because implementers and governance tools would still lack a clear base expectation that non-special identifiers be absolute references. The alternative avoids some policy friction but carries an interoperability cost by allowing ambiguous system namespaces to persist.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Reduces perceived conformance pressure on existing local identifiers, but preserves ambiguity and weakens a uniform base expectation for code system identity.

evidence.detail: R4 guidance says other URIs should reference a definition establishing the system clearly and unambiguously.
evidence.quote: it should reference to some definition

evidence.detail: R6 guidance says other URIs should be absolute references to such a definition.
evidence.quote: it should be an absolute reference to some definition

evidence.detail: The element remains type `uri` with cardinality 0..1, so no local schema-level type narrowing accompanies the text change.

examples.examplesMd: The example is illustrative rather than a full validation claim. The R6 base StructureDefinition does not add a hard validator rule for absolute URIs, but the R6 comment makes the relative/local `system` value a conformance and governance risk.

findings.narrativeMd: `Coding.system` is the namespace for interpreting `Coding.code`. R6 keeps the same field but clarifies that non-special identifiers should be absolute references. Implementers with local aliases or relative strings in `system` may not see parser errors, but their data may fail stricter R6 terminology governance or interoperability review.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: There is no old-valid/new-invalid schema break because the type remains `uri`, cardinality remains 0..1, and no invariant was added. The compatibility issue is behavioral: validators or linters that enforce specification comments can start warning or failing local identifiers. R6 values using absolute URIs are representable in R4 without loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory `Coding.system` values and identify local, relative, or environment-specific aliases. Replace them with stable absolute URIs only when the mapping preserves code identity; changing `system` changes the meaning namespace for every `code`. Maintain alias maps, update terminology services, and test round trips so old and new identifiers do not accidentally merge distinct code systems.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The clarification was probably justified to improve global interoperability. A more backward-compatible approach would have been separate guidance rather than changing the element comment, but the lack of a hard computable constraint keeps the practical disruption low.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is needed before rewriting `system` values because a syntactic normalization can become a semantic remapping of coded data.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 changes the `Coding.system` comment from saying non-OID/UUID systems should reference a clear definition to saying they should be an absolute reference to that definition. The element remains `uri` with cardinality 0..1 and no new invariant, regex, binding, or type narrowing. This is useful conformance clarification around stable code-system identity, but by itself it does not invalidate R4 instances or change generated model shape.
keyEvidence: R4 `Coding.system` is 0..1 type `uri` and says other URIs should reference a definition establishing the system clearly and unambiguously.
R6 `Coding.system` remains 0..1 type `uri` and changes the comment to say the URI should be an absolute reference to such a definition.
R6 `Coding.system` has only inherited `ele-1`; no computable absolute-URI invariant or type change accompanies the prose.
Package indexes confirm the compared artifacts are `StructureDefinition-Coding.json` for R4 4.0.1 and R6 6.0.0-ballot4.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Coding's normative R4 status raises sensitivity to true compatibility breaks, but here the change is non-computable guidance rather than a structural or validation restriction. Normative status does not turn this prose clarification into a hard migration problem.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: the base structure and validation constraints are unchanged; only the explanatory comment strengthens the recommended interpretation of `Coding.system` identifiers.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Retaining the R4 wording would be less textually disruptive, but it would also preserve ambiguity about relative/local system identifiers. Because the R6 change is prose-only and supports clearer terminology identity, there is no meaningful less-breaking base design issue.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing impact and alternative judgment: the prior report treats this as no hard break with at most low policy/terminology-governance risk, and I find no base-model compatibility problem requiring a different alternative assessment.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R6 artifact has the same id, URL, type, kind, status, and abstract flag. The baseDefinition changed from `Element` to `DataType`, but that is excluded as a global datatype hierarchy issue.
The local Coding elements `system`, `version`, `code`, `display`, and `userSelected` are present in both R4 and R6. No local element was added, removed, renamed, split, or merged.
Root `Coding` remains 0..* in the StructureDefinition, and each local child element remains 0..1.
`system` remains `uri`, `version` remains `string`, `code` remains `code`, `display` remains `string`, and `userSelected` remains `boolean`.
Coding has no Reference-typed local elements in either version.
No local ElementDefinition.binding is present on Coding elements in either version; there is therefore no local binding strength or value set change.
No local fixed, pattern, or default value constraints were found in either version.
No local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue limit changes were found.
No local Coding element became a modifier and no modifier reason was introduced.
The local data-bearing children remain summary elements in both versions.
No local Coding slicing changes were found. Inherited extension slicing is out of scope.
The JSON/XML element names and primitive types for local Coding content are unchanged. The R6 changes affect validation warnings and conformance text, not wire shape.
R6 adds no local instance element or local type alternative that R4 cannot carry. R6-valid Coding content using the same local elements is structurally representable in R4.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds datatype metadata characteristics for binding and translation tooling
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds StructureDefinition metadata extensions such as `structuredefinition-type-characteristics` values `can-bind` and `do-translations`. These are metadata about the datatype, not instance elements or validation rules for existing Coding JSON/XML content.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Terminology-aware authoring tools, profile tooling, and code generators may use these extensions to recognize Coding as bindable and translation-relevant. Tooling should treat them as capability metadata, not as new required instance fields.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 annotates Coding.code with a tooling no-binding extension
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `Coding.code` still has no ElementDefinition.binding and still has type `code`. The R6 `http://hl7.org/fhir/tools/StructureDefinition/no-binding` extension is a tooling annotation, not an instance constraint.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Profile authoring or code generation tools that inspect StructureDefinition extensions may need to recognize this annotation so they do not infer a direct value set binding on the primitive `code` child.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 preserves normative status but no longer carries the same normative-version extension shape
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Both versions mark Coding as normative, and this metadata does not change instance validity. The R4 StructureDefinition included a `structuredefinition-normative-version` extension with value `4.0.0`; the R6 top-level metadata observed in the package retains standards status but uses a different extension set.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tools that make maturity or standards-status decisions by looking for the exact R4 normative-version extension should be checked against R6 metadata conventions.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 `Coding` specializes `DataType` rather than `Element`. Per the assignment's inherited/base-artifact rule, this global datatype hierarchy change should be assessed in the DataType/base infrastructure report, not as a local Coding finding.
Observed differences on inherited `id`, `extension`, and inherited constraints are excluded here and should be resolved by Element/DataType/Extension analyses if they are material across datatypes.
